name: Add Item Button
summary: The full-width "+ Add" affordance that sits under a settings list (OptionRow / QuestionList) — the DS secondary Button at full width, appending a new item.
highlights: Full-width “+ Add” row under a settings list
The DS secondary Button, medium, full width
Appends a new item to OptionRow or QuestionList
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-add-item-button> — defined once, imported unchanged by React and Vue. It is the full-width add row beneath an editable list, and it IS the DS secondary Button (<aha-button variant="secondary" size="md" block>): white fill, 1px #E3E3E3 border, radius 8, 36 high, a leading system-plus glyph + the label in Plus Jakarta 14/600 default text. Hover, press, keyboard focus and disabled are the Button's own states, so the add row never drifts from the Button. Click emits a composed `add` event so the host can append an item; when the list hits its max count the host sets `disabled`. The `+` is decorative; the label carries the accessible name. Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens.
codeNote: Composes <aha-button variant="secondary" size="md" block> — no own button styling. React consumes it via a thin ref wrapper; Vue binds the custom element natively. Defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

whenToUse.when: append a new row to an editable settings list — options, questions, list items
a standalone action that isn't 'add another row to this list'

opinion.note: Place it directly under the list it grows, full-width so it reads as part of the stack. Label it with the item noun — 'Add option', 'Add question' — not a bare 'Add' when the context needs it. Disable (don't hide) it at the max count so the ceiling stays discoverable; pair with a tooltip or helper line explaining the limit.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — the settings option-list 'Add' row: the DS secondary Button at full width under OptionRow / QuestionList lists, matching the settings lab's Add question button (36 high, 1px #E3E3E3, 14/600).
